A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Privacy-Aware Visual Language Models study. Their main text, tables, figures, equations and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original VLM benchmark evaluations, privacy-tuning experiments, generalization and training-data analyses, multilingual comparisons and analysis of Places365.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark and privacy-tuning results, additional evaluations on existing privacy datasets, human label assessments, dataset audits and Places365 analysis.

M1.justification: The TinyLLaVA LoRA tuning approach remains, but dialogue supervision changes from mandatory 1–5 privacy scores to binary private/public explanations. The fallback annotation model for GPT-rejected nudity changes from MoELLaVA to ShareGPT4V, called ShareGPT in v2. These are limited revisions to the existing supervision pipeline.

E1.justification: v2 adds actual evaluations on PrivacyAlert and Biv-Priv, which v1 only discusses, and removes GQA evaluation. The three proposed datasets retain their eight sensitive categories, but their reported source changes from Flickr/Google/CC12M to Re-LAION. Hard negatives, four query languages and Places365 remain covered.

E2.justification: v2 Tables 2 and 9 expand the PRIVBENCH-H comparison from v1 Table 6's restricted set to all ten zero-shot baselines, adding participants such as BLIP, CogVLM, LLaVA and untuned TinyLLaVA. The tuned MiniGPT-v2 variant disappears. GPT-4V/GPT-4 and ShareGPT4V/ShareGPT are matched renamings.

E3.justification: Five-level prompting and AUC-ROC are replaced by Yes/No classification and F1, with additional precision, recall and accuracy reporting. Invalid responses change from excluded answers to mistakes, although v2 explicitly excludes GPT-4's rejected nudity samples. v2 also introduces external-dataset and human-evaluation protocols and increases the Places365 sample from 50,000 to 100,000 images.

E4.justification: v2 adds a class-definition prompting ablation and substantial dataset-quality analyses: human label validation, DETR person counts, CLIP-based diversity assessment and illustrated error audits. v1's criticism of existing datasets was largely unquantified. Leave-one-class-out, training-data sensitivity and multilingual analyses remain, while the repeated-subsample robustness analysis is removed.

E5.justification: v1 Appendix E reports means and standard deviations over 100 balanced random half-dataset splits; this benchmark uncertainty analysis disappears from v2. v2 introduces Fleiss' kappa for human annotation agreement. Dialogue-summary standard deviations remain, so uncertainty reporting is substantially revised rather than entirely removed.

E6.justification: Results are extensively replaced under revised data and scoring: tuned TinyLLaVA's PRIVBENCH result is 0.96 AUC-ROC in v1 Table 3 and 0.93 F1 in v2 Table 2, precluding direct performance comparison. New v2 Table 9 results include 0.62 F1 on PrivacyAlert and 0.67 on Biv-Priv, below MoELLaVA and CogVLM's 0.73 there. Human assessments, standard-task scores, generalization findings and Places365 rankings also change.

T1.justification: The formal privacy-score range changes from {1,2,3,4,5} to {0,1}, and v2 introduces a mathematical definition of CLIP-based class diversity in Section 4. The private-image-rate formula is retained. Neither version supplies theorems or proofs; the mathematical changes are limited.

C1.justification: The central benchmark and privacy-tuning contributions remain. Demonstrated tuning scope narrows from TinyLLaVA and MiniGPT-v2 to TinyLLaVA, while the introduction extends superiority claims to other privacy datasets. The conclusion strengthens 'without much compromising' standard-task performance to 'without compromising', despite decreases in v2 Table 4.

C2.justification: v2 develops the earlier text-versus-image discrepancy into a modality-misalignment interpretation supported by class-name prompting. It adds substantive explanations of existing datasets' label inconsistencies and limited diversity, GDPR-based justification of privacy categories, and acknowledgment that privacy extends beyond the selected classes. Dataset-ethics reasoning and documented safeguards are also revised.

D1.justification: v2 adds keyword-based collection instructions and detailed class-selection guidelines in Table 7, and revises licensing and removal-access information. Conversely, v1's exact evaluation prompts, inference token limit and hardware details disappear, as do the stated 80/20 training-validation split and several TinyLLaVA hyperparameters. These omissions do not establish changed underlying settings.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially repositioned around sensitive-attribute inference and reliable compact benchmarks, adding Staab et al., Tömekçe et al., ImageNet/CIFAR reevaluation work and tinyBenchmarks. Earlier discussion and citations concerning differential privacy, deduplication and copyright are removed. GDPR, the EU AI Act and Re-LAION also become explicit foundations.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, methodology, discussion and datasheet undergo extensive rewriting. Related work gains thematic subsections, multilingual evaluation moves from Discussion to Results, and detailed Places365 material moves into the supplement. Appendices are reorganized into numbered sections with a contents list.

P2.justification: The document changes from predominantly single-column to two-column layout. v2 replaces dialogue examples, adds human-agreement charts and extensive dataset-error galleries, consolidates standard and hard benchmark comparisons, and redesigns the standard-task table to show performance differences. Existing plots and prompt displays also receive changed labels, formatting or placement.

improvement.justification: External-dataset comparisons, human label assessments and explicit curation guidelines give v2's benchmark motivation and generalization claims stronger empirical grounding than v1's largely unsupported label-noise assertions. The net improvement is limited by removal of benchmark uncertainty estimates, a second tuned architecture and reproducibility details. The strengthened no-performance-loss conclusion also conflicts with v2 Table 4's reported decreases.
